Name of the Surah

• It is called Yusuf (Joseph), because it uniquely contains the complete story of the Prophet of Allah, Yusuf (peace be upon him); it is not mentioned in any other surah.

Some of the Objectives of the Surah

• Explaining the story of Yusuf with his brothers, and the wonderful narrative style it contains, and what it relates of their scheming against him, the trial of their casting him into the well, the separation from his parents, and the other hardships he faced in his life: enslavement, the scheming and seduction of the wife of the ruler (al-Aziz) through solicitation and enticement, and imprisonment after a life of comfort. All of this is a consolation to the Prophet (ﷺ) for what he suffered from the harm of relatives and strangers alike, and in it is solace for what the believer encounters from his own kin for holding fast to the law of Allah.

• Explaining the lesson in the patience of the prophets under trial, such as Ya'qub (Jacob) and Yusuf (peace be upon them both), and how the outcome was in their favor after trial and patience, and affirming the great kindness of Allah that He bestows upon His servants, and that what appears to us as trials which we may suppose to be calamities is in truth nothing but blessings.

• The call to monotheism (tawhid) in the darkest circumstances and the most difficult situations, as embodied in the Prophet Yusuf's doing so in the prison.

• Explaining that the interpretation of dreams (ta'bir al-ru'ya) is among the sciences that Allah bestows upon whomever He wills of His servants; it is one of the foundations of prophethood and a kind of legal opinion (fatwa). It also points out that among dreams are some that contain good news or a warning about a specific matter.

• Reviewing a number of aspects of the history of ancient civilization, its laws and its commerce, such as the enslavement of the thief, the conditions of prisoners, the monitoring of measures, and other things.

• Taking a lesson from the migration of the people of a prophet to the land in which they settle, as Ya'qub and his family did; and in this is a hint to believers that they should migrate to the Prophetic city (Madinah) as emigrants, following the migration of the Prophet (ﷺ).

[The Tafsir]

﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾ The discussion of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah) has already been given at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah. These are the verses of the Book that is clear in its meanings, its lawful and unlawful matters, and its guidance.
We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an, so that you, O Arabs, may understand its meanings and comprehend them, and act upon its guidance.

We relate to you, O Messenger, the best of stories through Our revelation to you of this Qur'an, though before its revelation to you, you were certainly among those unaware of these accounts, knowing nothing of them.

Mention, O Messenger, to your people the words of Yusuf to his father: "Indeed, I saw in a dream eleven stars, and the sun and the moon—I saw them prostrating to me." This dream was a glad tidings of the exalted station that Yusuf (peace be upon him) would attain in this world and the Hereafter.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 12, verse 5:

And just as your Lord has shown you this vision, so He will choose you, teach you the interpretation of dreams and visions, the outcome to which they lead in reality, and He will complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Ya'qub (Jacob) with prophethood and messengerhood, just as He completed it before upon your two forefathers, Ibrahim (Abraham) and Ishaq (Isaac), with prophethood and messengerhood. Surely there were lessons and signs in the story of Yusuf and his brothers, proofs of Allah's power and wisdom, for those who ask about their news and desire to know it.

When Joseph's brothers said among themselves: "Joseph and his full brother are dearer to our father than we are, though we are a group of strong men. Indeed, our father is in clear error, for he favors them over us without any reason we can see."

The one who had come for water and his companions concealed Joseph from the rest of the travelers and did not show him to them, and they said: "This is merchandise that we have acquired (istibda'na)." He said to them: "Rather, your own souls, which command to evil, have made a scheme attractive to you, which you devised, just as you did before with Joseph. So my patience is a beautiful patience, with no complaint and no lamentation accompanying it. Perhaps Allah will return to me my three sons—namely Joseph, his full brother, and their eldest brother who stayed behind for his brother's sake—for He is indeed the All-Knowing of my condition, the All-Wise in His management."

Jacob turned away from them, his chest constricted by what they had said, and he said: "Alas, my grief for Joseph!" His eyes turned white, their blackness having gone from intense sorrow. He was filled with grief at heart, yet he was very restrained in concealing it.
His sons said: "By Allah, you will not stop remembering Joseph, and your grief over him will keep increasing until you come close to destruction or actually perish, so ease your soul."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 12, verse 86:

Ya'qub (ʿAlayhi al-Salam) said in reply to them: I do not complain of my grief and sorrow except to Allah alone, for He is the One who removes harm and affliction, and I know from the mercy of Allah and His relief what you do not know.

Ya'qub said: "O my sons, go back to Egypt and seek out news of Yusuf and his brother, and do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, none despairs of the mercy of Allah except the disbelievers who deny His power and reject Him."

They went to "Egypt" for the third time. When they entered upon Yusuf, they said: "O Chief (al-'Aziz), hardship and famine have struck us and our families, and we have come to you with inferior, meager merchandise. So give us full measure with it, as you used to give us with good currency before, and be charitable to us by accepting these inferior, meager dirhams, and overlook it for us. Indeed, Allah rewards those who give charity with their wealth to those in need."

When he heard their words, he felt pity for them and made himself known to them, and said: "Do you remember what you did to Joseph and his brother, in your ignorance of the outcome of what you were doing?"

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 12, verse 90:

They said, "Are you truly Joseph?" He said, "Yes, I am Joseph, and this is my full brother. God has shown favor to us and brought us together after separation. Indeed, whoever fears God and is patient in trials, then God does not waste the reward of the good-doers, but He rewards them with the best reward."

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 12, verse 91:

They said: "By Allah, Allah has certainly preferred you over us, and has honored you with knowledge, forbearance and virtue. Indeed, we were sinners in what we did to you and your brother deliberately."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 12, verse 92:

Yusuf said to them: "There is no reproach upon you today. May Allah forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful to whoever repents of his sin and turns back to His obedience."

When he asked them about his father, they told him that his sight had gone from weeping over him. He said to them: "Go back to your father, and take with you this shirt of mine. Cast it over my father's face, and his sight will return to him. Then bring me all your family."

When the caravan had left the land of Egypt, heading for Syria, carrying the shirt, Ya'qub (Jacob) said to those present with him: "Indeed, I sense the scent of Yusuf (Joseph) and his shirt, were it not that you would deem me foolish and mock me, and think that these words came from me without awareness."
Those present with him said: "By God, you are still in your old error of loving Joseph, and you do not forget him."

When the bearer of good news came to Ya'qub, telling him that Yusuf was alive, and threw the shirt of Yusuf over his face, Ya'qub regained his sight, and joy overwhelmed him. He said to those around him: "Did I not tell you that I know from Allah what you do not know, of His bounty, His mercy and His generosity?"
His sons said: "O our father, ask your Lord to forgive us and to cover over our sins, for we were sinners in what we did to Joseph and his full brother."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 12, verse 98:

Jacob said: "I will ask my Lord to forgive you your sins. Indeed, He is the Forgiving toward the sins of His servants who repent, the Merciful toward them."

Ya'qub and his family set out for Egypt, seeking Yusuf. When they reached him, Yusuf drew his two parents close to him and said to them: "Enter Egypt, if Allah wills, and you will be safe from hardship, famine, and every harm."

She seated his parents upon the throne beside him, showing them honour. His parents and his eleven brothers bowed down before him in greeting and reverence, not in worship and submission. Such prostration was permissible in their law, but it has been forbidden in our law, as a means of blocking the path to associating partners with God.

Yusuf said to his father: "This prostration is the interpretation of my dream which I related to you before, in my youth. My Lord has made it come true. He has been gracious to me when He brought me out of prison and brought you all to me from the desert, after Satan had spoiled the bond of brotherhood between me and my brothers. Indeed my Lord is Subtle in arranging whatever He wills; indeed He is the All-Knowing of His servants' interests, the All-Wise in His sayings and His doings."

Then Yusuf supplicated his Lord, saying: "My Lord, You have indeed granted me of the kingdom (of Egypt), and taught me of the interpretation of dreams (ta'wil al-ru'a) and other knowledge. O Creator of the heavens and the earth and their Originator, You are the Guardian of all my affairs in this world and the Hereafter. Cause me to die in submission (to You), and join me with Your righteous servants, the virtuous prophets and the chosen good ones."

That story of Joseph which has been mentioned is among the reports of the unseen (akhbar al-ghayb) that We inform you of, O Messenger, by revelation. You were not present with Joseph's brothers when they devised their plan to throw him into the well, and when they schemed against him and against his father. This indicates your truthfulness, and that Allah reveals to you.
And most of the people, O Messenger, will not believe you nor follow you, even if you were eager for their faith; so do not grieve over that.

And you do not ask your people for any wage for guiding them to faith. Indeed, what you were sent with, the Qur'an and guidance, is a reminder for all people, through which they remember and are guided.

And many of the signs that point to God's oneness and His power are spread throughout the heavens and the earth, such as the sun, the moon, the mountains and the trees. They see them, yet they turn away from them, neither reflecting upon them nor taking heed.

Most of those who turn away from the signs of God do not acknowledge that God is their Creator, their Provider, and the Creator of everything, except that they are associating others with Him in worship, through their worship of idols and images. Exalted is God far above that, by a great exaltation.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 12, verse 107:

Do they then feel secure that there will not come upon them a punishment from Allah that overwhelms them in this world, or that the Hour will not come upon them suddenly while they are unaware and do not perceive it?

Say, [O Messenger], to them: "This is my way: I call to the worship of Allah alone, upon clear proof and certainty, I and whoever follows me. And I exalt Allah, glorified and exalted is He, above partners, and I am not among those who associate others with Allah."

This is the commentary on Surah Yusuf (12), verse 109.

And We did not send before you, [O Messenger], to the people except men from among them to whom We revealed. And they were from the people of the settled towns, for they are more capable of understanding the call and the message. Those who are guided to the truth believe them, and those who stray from it deny them. Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those who denied before them, and what destruction befell them? And the reward of the Hereafter is better than this world and what is in it, for those who believe and fear their Lord. Will you not then reason and take heed?

Do not hasten, O Messenger, the victory over those who deny you. Indeed, the messengers before you did not have victory come to them quickly, for a wisdom We know. Until, when the messengers despaired of their people's faith, and those to whom they were sent thought that the messengers had lied to them concerning what they reported from Allah, Our victory came to Our messengers at the height of distress. So We saved whom We willed of the messengers and their followers, and Our punishment is not turned back from the people who committed crime and dared against Allah. In this there is consolation for the Prophet (ﷺ).

Indeed, in the accounts of the messengers that We have related to you, and in what befell those who denied them, there is a lesson for people of sound minds. This Qur'an is not a fabricated, invented narration. Rather, We sent it down as a confirmation of the truth of the scriptures revealed before it, and of their being from Allah, and as an explanation of everything the servants need concerning what is permitted and what is forbidden, what is beloved and what is disliked, and other matters, and as guidance away from misguidance, and as a mercy for the people of faith, by which their hearts are guided, so that they act upon its commands and prohibitions.
